titleCard.title: Sift
titleCard.subtitle: Twelve bids for the same job. The low one is $52,500 under the winner. Is it a better deal, or is it pricing less work?

closeCard.title: The agent recommends. The human decides.
closeCard.subtitle: Real Strands Swarm, AgentSkills, Context Injection and GoalLoop - with a deterministic core the model never touches.

beats.title: Twelve bids, and no estimator
lines: Meridian Builders is a nine-person general contractor, and nobody there is a full-time estimator.
They put a school plumbing package out to the regional plan room, and twelve bids came back.
The person picking this sub is also running the job.

beats.title: Twelve bids, and no estimator
lines: Twelve bids is where you stop reading and sort by the bottom number.
And that is the trap. Cedar and Sons prices sixty-two and a half percent of the required scope. Northgate prices all of it.
Is the cheap bid a better deal, or is it pricing less work?

beats.title: A real Swarm, and it gets steered
lines: Six specialists, and the handoffs are the model's decision, not a script.
Scope, price, credentials, schedule, a source check, and a recommendation - each loading only the skill its own obligation needs.
Watch the scope analyst. It finishes: completed, redirected once.
It was comparing the same two bids again with no new angle, so the run steered it onto the third.
That is a Guide intervention, landing on a live handoff.
Every specialist reports what it actually did - nine price lookups, two credential lookups, five on schedule.

beats.title: Blocked, then refused
lines: This is the run's own activity stream, and two entries in it are the whole submission.

beats.title: Blocked, then refused
lines: Action blocked. The price analyst reached for the licence lookup - a tool that is not in its allowlist for this run.
Not a failure. A refusal, recorded as one, and the run carried straight on without it.

beats.title: Blocked, then refused
lines: And then this. Draft withheld - recommendation draft rejected on attempt one.
The validator threw out the first answer because Cedar's scope was not normalized yet, and ranking twelve bids on different scope bases would have been a lie.
Every bid-levelling tool will happily rank an unfair comparison. This one refused, and went back round.

beats.title: Arithmetic you can check yourself
lines: Cedar's two-twenty-three-five is silent on three things the others price.
Permits and inspections, eighteen thousand. Shower-valve rough-in, thirty-one five. Debris haul-away, six thousand.
Add them: Cedar is two seventy-nine, against Northgate's two seventy-six.
The bid that looked fifty-two thousand cheaper is three thousand more expensive - arithmetic you can check yourself.
And the one bid genuinely under Northgate once corrected, Fieldstone at two sixty-eight, doesn't win either. It tells you why.

beats.title: It won't call two questions closed
lines: It recommended a winner and it still won't mark two of these questions answered.
Cedar's scope comparison came back incomplete, and two of the twelve fail credential verification on two different grounds.
A certificate naming the wrong company, and a licence class with no plumbing endorsement.
Evidence here is fail-closed: a degraded answer doesn't get to count as settled just because everything else passed.

beats.title: A constraint that outranks a score
lines: Say you care less about price and more about warranty and a sane deposit.
Change the weights - the ranking is arithmetic the model never touches.
And the sixth criterion has no slider: credentials are set by the pack and cannot be reweighted.

beats.title: A constraint that outranks a score
lines: Save it, and only the question the reweight actually affects reopens - one specialist, one revised pass.

beats.title: A constraint that outranks a score
lines: And now Two Rivers scores highest of all twelve - ninety-one percent, against the winner's seventy-two.

beats.title: A constraint that outranks a score
lines: It still doesn't win. Its insurance names TRM Holdings, not Two Rivers Mechanical, and credentials are a hard constraint.
Eleventh of twelve, ninety-one percent still showing, and it says: flagged, not removed - still ranked, and still yours to decide.

beats.title: It recommends; it never awards
lines: Awarding a contract is real money leaving a real business.
So this is gated - a Confirm intervention, and the proposal sits pending with no approving actor until a person acts.
The agent got to recommend. I'm the one who awards.
That boundary is structural, not a setting I could switch off.

beats.title: Proof it is really Strands
lines: And underneath, everything you just watched is real Strands.
Four hundred and thirty-three runtime events in that first run: six swarm nodes, six stages, five handoffs.

beats.title: Proof it is really Strands
lines: Twenty-eight context injections, four skill activations, and every span carrying the SDK's own instrumentation scope.
Which is the one thing a class you named after Strands cannot fake.

beats.title: Optimized to know when it hasn't earned an answer
lines: Most agents are optimized to finish.
This one is optimized to know when it hasn't earned the right to answer yet.
